questions.stem: Which suffix in an organic compound's name indicates it belongs to the alcohol homologous series?
questions.explanation: The suffix -ol indicates an alcohol. For example, ethanol and propanol are alcohols. The suffix -ane indicates alkanes, -ene indicates alkenes, and -oic acid indicates carboxylic acids.

questions.stem: A hydrocarbon that contains only single carbon-carbon bonds is described as:
questions.explanation: A saturated hydrocarbon contains only single carbon-carbon bonds, meaning each carbon is bonded to the maximum number of hydrogen atoms. Alkanes are saturated. Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one C=C double bond, such as alkenes.
